nodes.name: Generator $G$
nodes.statement: $G(\bm{z}; \theta_g)$ is a differentiable function (multilayer perceptron with parameters $\theta_g$) mapping noise $\bm{z} \sim p_{\bm{z}}$ to data space, defining an implicit distribution $p_g$ over data $\bm{x}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Generator network: a differentiable mapping from noise to data, implicitly defining the model distribution $p_g$.

nodes.name: Discriminator $D$
nodes.statement: $D(\bm{x}; \theta_d)$ is a multilayer perceptron outputting a single scalar; $D(\bm{x})$ represents the probability that $\bm{x}$ came from the data distribution rather than from $p_g$.
nodes.statement_clean: Discriminator network: a scalar-valued classifier estimating $P(\text{real} \mid \bm{x})$.

nodes.name: Adversarial value function $V(G,D)$
nodes.statement: The two-player minimax value function is $V(D,G) = \mathbb{E}_{\bm{x} \sim p_{\text{data}}}[\log D(\bm{x})] + \mathbb{E}_{\bm{z} \sim p_{\bm{z}}}[\log (1 - D(G(\bm{z})))]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Defines the adversarial objective combining discriminator log-likelihood on real and generated samples.

nodes.name: Virtual training criterion $C(G)$
nodes.statement: $C(G) = \max_D V(G,D) = \mathbb{E}_{\bm{x} \sim p_{\text{data}}}[\log D^*_G(\bm{x})] + \mathbb{E}_{\bm{x} \sim p_g}[\log (1 - D^*_G(\bm{x}))]$.
nodes.statement_clean: The generator's objective after maximizing out the discriminator.

nodes.name: Jensen-Shannon divergence
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{JSD}(p \| q) = \tfrac{1}{2} \mathrm{KL}(p \| \tfrac{p+q}{2}) + \tfrac{1}{2} \mathrm{KL}(q \| \tfrac{p+q}{2})$, a symmetric, non-negative divergence between distributions, zero iff $p=q$.
nodes.statement_clean: Symmetrized KL divergence used to characterize the GAN global optimum.

nodes.name: Adversarial minimax game
nodes.statement: $\min_G \max_D V(D,G) = \mathbb{E}_{\bm{x} \sim p_{\text{data}}}[\log D(\bm{x})] + \mathbb{E}_{\bm{z} \sim p_{\bm{z}}}[\log (1 - D(G(\bm{z})))]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Train $G$ and $D$ as adversaries: $G$ minimizes while $D$ maximizes the value function.

nodes.name: Minimax game definition
nodes.statement: $\min_G \max_D V(D,G) = \mathbb{E}_{\bm{x} \sim p_{\text{data}}(\bm{x})}[\log D(\bm{x})] + \mathbb{E}_{\bm{z} \sim p_{\bm{z}}(\bm{z})}[\log (1 - D(G(\bm{z})))]$.

nodes.name: Optimal discriminator form
nodes.statement: $D^*_G(\bm{x}) = \dfrac{p_{\text{data}}(\bm{x})}{p_{\text{data}}(\bm{x}) + p_g(\bm{x})}$.

nodes.name: $C(G)$ as JSD
nodes.statement: $C(G) = -\log 4 + 2 \cdot \mathrm{JSD}(p_{\text{data}} \| p_g)$.

nodes.name: Optimal discriminator for fixed $G$
nodes.statement: For $G$ fixed, the optimal discriminator $D$ is $D^*_G(\bm{x}) = \dfrac{p_{\text{data}}(\bm{x})}{p_{\text{data}}(\bm{x}) + p_g(\bm{x})}$.
assumptions: $p_{\text{data}}, p_g$ are densities on the data space

nodes.name: Global optimum of $C(G)$
nodes.statement: The global minimum of the virtual training criterion $C(G)$ is achieved if and only if $p_g = p_{\text{data}}$. At that point, $C(G)$ achieves the value $-\log 4$.
conclusions: the minimum is attained iff $p_g = p_{\text{data}}$

nodes.name: Convergence of Algorithm 1
nodes.statement: If $G$ and $D$ have enough capacity, and at each step the discriminator reaches its optimum given $G$, and $p_g$ is updated so as to improve $\mathbb{E}_{\bm{x} \sim p_{\text{data}}}[\log D^*_G(\bm{x})] + \mathbb{E}_{\bm{x} \sim p_g}[\log (1 - D^*_G(\bm{x}))]$, then $p_g$ converges to $p_{\text{data}}$.
assumptions: discriminator reaches its optimum at each step given current $G$
$p_g$ is updated to improve the criterion at the optimal $D$

nodes.name: Minibatch SGD training of generative adversarial nets
nodes.statement: Iterative minibatch stochastic gradient descent that alternates $k$ discriminator updates with one generator update on the minimax objective.
input: Hyperparameter $k$ (number of discriminator steps per generator step)

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1 (optimal discriminator)
nodes.statement: Rewrite $V(G,D)$ as an integral $\int p_{\text{data}}(\bm{x}) \log D(\bm{x}) + p_g(\bm{x}) \log(1-D(\bm{x})) d\bm{x}$, then maximize the integrand pointwise using that $y \mapsto a \log y + b \log(1-y)$ is maximized at $y = a/(a+b)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1 (global optimum)
nodes.statement: Compute $C(G)$ at $p_g = p_{\text{data}}$ giving $-\log 4$; rewrite $C(G) - (-\log 4)$ as the sum of two KL divergences, recognize as $2 \cdot \mathrm{JSD}(p_{\text{data}} \| p_g)$, and use non-negativity of JSD with equality iff $p_g = p_{\text{data}}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2 (convergence)
nodes.statement: View $V(G,D) = U(p_g, D)$ as a function of $p_g$; $U$ is convex in $p_g$, and a subderivative of the supremum of convex functions includes the derivative at the attained maximum, so updating $p_g$ at the optimal $D$ is a (sub)gradient step on the convex function $\sup_D U(p_g, D)$, which by Theorem 1 has unique global optimum at $p_g = p_{\text{data}}$.

nodes.name: MNIST, TFD, and CIFAR-10 experiments
nodes.statement: Adversarial nets trained on MNIST, the Toronto Face Database, and CIFAR-10; samples evaluated by Gaussian Parzen-window log-likelihood on the test set, achieving $225 \pm 2$ on MNIST and $2057 \pm 26$ on TFD.

nodes.name: Non-saturating generator objective
nodes.statement: Early in learning $\log(1 - D(G(\bm{z})))$ saturates because $D$ rejects $G$'s samples confidently; instead, train $G$ to maximize $\log D(G(\bm{z}))$, which has the same fixed point but provides much stronger gradients.

nodes.name: Helvetica scenario / mode collapse
nodes.statement: If $G$ is trained too much without updating $D$, $G$ may collapse many values of $\bm{z}$ to the same value of $\bm{x}$, reducing diversity and failing to model $p_{\text{data}}$.

nodes.name: Parametric optimization caveat
nodes.statement: In practice $G(\bm{z}; \theta_g)$ defines a limited parametric family and one optimizes $\theta_g$, not $p_g$ itself; this introduces multiple critical points and removes the theoretical guarantee, but multilayer perceptrons perform well empirically.

nodes.name: Rewrite $V(G,D)$ as an $\bm{x}$-integral
nodes.statement: By change of variables $\bm{x} = G(\bm{z})$, $V(G,D) = \int_{\bm{x}} p_{\text{data}}(\bm{x}) \log D(\bm{x}) + p_g(\bm{x}) \log(1 - D(\bm{x})) d\bm{x}$.

nodes.name: Pointwise maximization of integrand
nodes.statement: For any $(a,b) \in \mathbb{R}^2 \setminus \{0,0\}$, $y \mapsto a \log y + b \log(1-y)$ achieves its maximum on $[0,1]$ at $y^* = a/(a+b)$.

nodes.name: Conclude optimal $D^*_G$
nodes.statement: Setting $a = p_{\text{data}}(\bm{x})$, $b = p_g(\bm{x})$ pointwise yields $D^*_G(\bm{x}) = p_{\text{data}}(\bm{x}) / (p_{\text{data}}(\bm{x}) + p_g(\bm{x}))$ on $\mathrm{Supp}(p_{\text{data}}) \cup \mathrm{Supp}(p_g)$.

nodes.name: Evaluate $C(G)$ at $p_g = p_{\text{data}}$
nodes.statement: If $p_g = p_{\text{data}}$ then $D^*_G(\bm{x}) = 1/2$, so $C(G) = \log\tfrac{1}{2} + \log\tfrac{1}{2} = -\log 4$.

nodes.name: Subtract the constant $-\log 4$ from $C(G)$
nodes.statement: Using $\mathbb{E}_{\bm{x} \sim p_{\text{data}}}[-\log 2] + \mathbb{E}_{\bm{x} \sim p_g}[-\log 2] = -\log 4$, subtract this from $C(G)$ to obtain $C(G) = -\log 4 + \mathrm{KL}(p_{\text{data}} \| \tfrac{p_{\text{data}}+p_g}{2}) + \mathrm{KL}(p_g \| \tfrac{p_{\text{data}}+p_g}{2})$.

nodes.name: Identify the JSD
nodes.statement: Recognize the sum of KL terms as $2 \cdot \mathrm{JSD}(p_{\text{data}} \| p_g)$, giving $C(G) = -\log 4 + 2 \cdot \mathrm{JSD}(p_{\text{data}} \| p_g)$.

nodes.name: Conclude global minimum
nodes.statement: Since $\mathrm{JSD} \ge 0$ with equality iff $p_g = p_{\text{data}}$, the global minimum $C^* = -\log 4$ is attained uniquely at $p_g = p_{\text{data}}$.

nodes.name: Reformulate $V$ as $U(p_g, D)$ convex in $p_g$
nodes.statement: View $V(G,D) = U(p_g, D)$; then $U(p_g, D)$ is convex in $p_g$ for every $D$.

nodes.name: Subgradient of supremum of convex functions
nodes.statement: If $f(x) = \sup_{\alpha \in \mathcal{A}} f_\alpha(x)$ with each $f_\alpha$ convex in $x$, then $\partial f_\beta(x) \subseteq \partial f(x)$ when $\beta = \arg\sup_\alpha f_\alpha(x)$; thus updating $p_g$ at the optimal $D$ is a subgradient step on $\sup_D U(p_g, D)$.

nodes.name: Use uniqueness of global optimum
nodes.statement: $\sup_D U(p_g, D)$ is convex in $p_g$ with a unique global optimum at $p_g = p_{\text{data}}$ by Theorem 1; therefore with sufficiently small updates, $p_g$ converges to $p_{\text{data}}$.

nodes.name: Outer training loop
nodes.statement: For number of training iterations: do the inner discriminator updates, then a generator update.

nodes.name: Inner discriminator update loop
nodes.statement: For $k$ steps: sample minibatch of $m$ noise samples $\{\bm{z}^{(1)}, \dots, \bm{z}^{(m)}\}$ from $p_g(\bm{z})$ and $m$ examples $\{\bm{x}^{(1)}, \dots, \bm{x}^{(m)}\}$ from $p_{\text{data}}$.

nodes.name: Discriminator gradient ascent
nodes.statement: Update $\theta_d$ by ascending the stochastic gradient $\nabla_{\theta_d} \tfrac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \left[\log D(\bm{x}^{(i)}) + \log(1 - D(G(\bm{z}^{(i)})))\right]$.

nodes.name: Sample noise for generator step
nodes.statement: Sample minibatch of $m$ noise samples $\{\bm{z}^{(1)}, \dots, \bm{z}^{(m)}\}$ from $p_g(\bm{z})$.

nodes.name: Generator gradient descent
nodes.statement: Update $\theta_g$ by descending the stochastic gradient $\nabla_{\theta_g} \tfrac{1}{m} \sum_{i=1}^m \log(1 - D(G(\bm{z}^{(i)})))$.
